oewn-00415192-n.learner: a way of acting that you fall into without thinking in a certain situation, which you may be born with or may learn by doing it again and again
examples: Long use had hardened him to the cold of the early mornings.

oewn-05197374-n.learner: the act of using your legal right to enjoy the good things that come from owning property
examples: We were given the use of his boat for the summer.

oewn-13472977-n.learner: the using up of goods to meet people's needs, or to make other things
examples: Water use in the town rises sharply every summer.

oewn-00159005-n.learner: using clever or sly ways to control people, especially to get something for yourself
examples: He was skilled in the use of other people for his own gain.

connotation.why: implies working on people slyly for one's own advantage

oewn-07232009-n.learner: the act of formally making a person known to someone else, or to the public
examples: I should have judged better had I sought an introduction, but I am ill-qualified to recommend myself to strangers.
Miss Darcy and her brother appeared, and this formidable introduction took place.

oewn-06408573-n.learner: the first part of something that is written or said
examples: The introduction of the book explains why the author wrote it.

oewn-00238889-n.learner: the act of starting something new
examples: The introduction of the new menu brought more people into the cafe.

oewn-00241051-n.learner: the act of starting something for the first time; bringing in something new
examples: The introduction of free schools changed life in the town.

oewn-07177626-n.learner: a new plan or idea that someone puts forward
examples: They resisted the introduction of impractical alternatives.

oewn-06426492-n.learner: a simple book or text that teaches the first, basic things about a subject
examples: She bought a short introduction to French grammar.

oewn-00321678-n.learner: the act of putting one thing into another
examples: The introduction of air into the pipe stopped the flow of water.

oewn-00758694-v.learner: to say something that you do not really mean
examples: He pretended he was happy for her, but he did not mean a word of it.

connotation.why: marks what someone says as insincere

oewn-01725433-v.learner: to behave in a way that is not natural, or in a false, put-on way
examples: Stop pretending and just talk to us the way you always do.

connotation.why: suggests the behaviour is false or put on

oewn-02280644-v.learner: to claim that you have a right to something, or that it belongs to you
examples: The young prince pretended to the throne his uncle held.

oewn-01320193-v.learner: to go looking for something, or to hunt for it
examples: He spent years pursuing the lost city deep in the jungle.
Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice
We dine at Rosings twice every week, and are never allowed to walk home.

oewn-00083743-r.learner: to double the amount or degree
examples: This box is twice as heavy as that one.

oewn-02047744-v.learner: to put something out so that it passes from person to person
examples: He was sent to prison for uttering false banknotes.

oewn-05781046-n.learner: a line of careful thinking meant to show that something is true or false; the step-by-step process of thinking logically
examples: Her argument moved step by step from the facts to a clear conclusion.

oewn-06479351-n.learner: a short account of the subject or the story of a book, poem, play or film
examples: The editor added the argument to the poem.

oewn-06367706-n.learner: a value, or a reference to one, that is passed to a function, command or program in computing
examples: This function takes two arguments and returns their sum.

oewn-05866365-n.learner: a variable in a logic or maths expression whose value decides the value of the variable that depends on it
examples: In the expression sin x, x is the argument of the function.

oewn-01132302-v.learner: to protect something against a challenge or an attack
examples: The champion guarded her title against every challenger.
He slept little the night before the exam.
She cared little for what the neighbours thought.

oewn-01060446-v.learner: to say or write a comment about something
examples: The critics noticed the play only briefly in their reviews.
